claims.claim: The review covers all 51 Lens best practices
claims.evidence: Script-extracted distinct IDs from review.md = 51, exactly equal to the 51 rows in assets/best-practices.csv. The 'Full assessment' table has one row per practice.

claims.claim: Pillar roll-up counts (Met 4 / Partial 7 / Not met 33 / N/A 7 = 51) are internally consistent with the per-practice table
claims.evidence: Totals sum to 51 and match the practice count. Per-pillar row counts (10/10/10/8/9/4) also match the Lens's per-pillar practice counts in best-practices.csv.

claims.claim: customer_id is documented in handler.py but never used
claims.evidence: Confirmed in the fixture: handler.py:3 docstring declares customer_id in the POST body; the token appears nowhere else in the file — handler() reads only body["question"] at line 44.

claims.claim: GENSEC05-BP01, GENREL03-BP02, GENREL05-BP03 and GENCOST05-BP01 are genuinely N/A because the workload has no agentic behaviour
claims.evidence: Justified correctly — handler.py performs exactly one retrieve() and one invoke_model() call with no tool use or action groups. The review also flags that adding agentic capability re-opens all four.

claims.claim: The Lambda timeout of 300s exceeds the API Gateway HTTP API 30s integration cap
claims.evidence: main.tf:55 sets timeout = 300; the 30s HTTP API integration cap is accurate AWS behaviour. Finding 7 draws the correct cost consequence (Bedrock keeps generating after the caller has a 504).

suggestions.assertion: Cites at least 8 distinct real Generative AI Lens best-practice IDs
suggestions.reason: This run cites all 51 IDs — i.e. it enumerates the entire Lens. A count threshold of 8 is trivially cleared by any output that pastes the practice table, and it cannot distinguish 'used the right practices' from 'listed every practice'. Consider asserting that the top-priority findings map to the correct practice, or capping breadth (e.g. 'the top 5 findings are the highest-risk ones for this workload').

suggestions.assertion: Includes a per-practice status table using Met / Partially met / Not met / Not applicable
suggestions.reason: The wording invites a string-match dispute: this run uses 'Partial' and 'N/A'. If the four-state vocabulary matters, say 'or recognisable abbreviations'; if it doesn't, drop the enumeration and assert that every practice has a status and that N/A verdicts carry justification.

No assertion checks that cited file/line evidence is actually correct. I verified handler.py:16/21/33/54, main.tf:110-113/140-143 and README:23-28 by hand and they were accurate — but a run that invents plausible line numbers would pass every current assertion. A 'cited line numbers resolve to the claimed content' assertion would be highly discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong eval set with good coverage of the fixture's planted defects. The main weakness is that ID-count assertions reward breadth over correct targeting.
